verdicts.summary: The quit-finalizer note's real hazard is the mutex wait before closeRun, which finding 0 already states. I confirmed it: the WSL configResolve path reaches prepareRuntime, so the 5s bound does not cover it. The note's failure-mode claim that the child may be left running is not reachable, because the close fiber SIGKILLs at 2s and the run fiber clears state later.
verdicts.scenario: Quit while a WSL backend's start holds the mutex in configResolve: stop() blocks at mutex.withPermits before closeRun, so the 5s timeout never starts. Covered by finding 0.

verdicts.summary: Tried: the drain (or any slow step) pushes closeRun past 5s while the child is still alive. The child cannot survive that, because the spawn release SIGKILLs it after forceKillAfter (2s) inside the forked close fiber, which timeoutOption does not cancel. The note's claim that the run is left uncleaned is also wrong: finalizeRun clears active, removeControlSource and discardSession once the run fiber finishes.
verdicts.scenario: Backend ignores SIGTERM and its stdout is held open, so the drain runs past the 5s timeout. Expected: child left alive and quit proceeds. Actual: the spawn release's timeoutOrElse sends SIGKILL at 2s (NodeChildProcessSpawner.ts:431-434, release at 484-511), inside closeFiber. Forked in parentScope (DesktopBackendManager.ts:366), so it keeps running after stop returns. The run fiber's finalizeRun then clears active, removeControlSource and discardSession, so nothing is left behind.
verdicts.consequence: Only a diagnostic gap: no log is emitted when the timeout trips (closeRun returns false silently). The process still exits after a SIGKILL. The timed-out close is not a leak. Assumes the desktop uses the node-shared spawner, which main.ts:218 NodeServices.layer provides.

verdicts.summary: The open question resolves as follows: prepareRuntime (363) is in runWslPreflight, called from resolveWslStartConfig (599). The worst case is also unbounded, not minutes. The mounted-tree fallback extracts the whole server tree with no timeout, and that runs under the start mutex.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Packaged Windows build, WSL-only mode. 2) The WSL runtime archive is missing or its hash is invalid (DesktopBackendConfiguration.ts:583-602), or prepareRuntime returns not-ok. Then runWslPreflight falls through to resolveMountedAppRoot (399), which calls wslServerTree.ensure. 3) On the packaged win32 path, ensure runs copyTree of the whole server tree (DesktopWslServerTree.ts:202-232, 90-117) with no timeout, while start holds the mutex (DesktopBackendManager.ts:692, 711). 4) The user quits during the copy. stop() blocks at the mutex (1051) and the 5s bound never applies. markComplete is not reached, and awaitComplete (DesktopShutdown.ts:30) has no timeout. The quit waits until the copy finishes on its own.
verdicts.consequence: The app does not quit (windows already destroyed, process lingers) for as long as the server-tree copy takes. That copy depends on disk and antivirus speed and has no upper bound. Finding 0's 'up to minutes' is therefore too narrow for this path. Pre-existing: stop() was unbounded before this commit too.
